THE REPORT OF THE GENERAL SECRETARY 
OF THE YOUNG MEN'S CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATION OF MONTREAL 
FOR THE YEAR ENDING MARCH 31st, 1931 


THE YOUNG MEN'S CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATION OF MONTREAL 

HAS NOW COMPLETED EIGHTY YEARS OF SERVICE, AND THE YEAR 
-JuS® GONE HAS, IN SOME RESPECTS, BEEN MOST NOTABLE OF Alto, 
THE GENERAL WORLD-WIDE ECONOMIC DEPRESSION, WHICH IS RE- 
PORTED TO SE ONE OF THE MOST SEVERE AND LONGEST CONTINUED 
IN RECORDED HISTORY, HAS THROWN UPON THE ASSOCIATION AN 
UNPRECEDENTEO DEMAND FOR SERVICE. UNLIKE MANY BUSINESS 
ORGANIZATIONS, THE YeMeCoA. IN TIMES OF DEPRESSION HAS 
EVEN MORE CALLS UPON IT THAN IN NORMAL YEARS. YOUNG MEN 
HAVE MORE LEISURE TIME ANO BECAUSE OF THE EXIGENCIES OF 
THE SITUATION, ARE MUCH MORE SERIOUS ABOUT THEIR USE OF 
1Te HUNOREDS OF THEM, OUT OF EMPLOYMENT, OR ONLY PART=- 
1ALLY EMPLOYED, COME TO THE "Y" WITH BAFFLING AND DIFF- 
CULT PROBLEMS OF ALMOST EVERY KIND; AND BOYS, WHO AT 
NORMAL TIMES REMAIN IN SCHOOL, ARE FORCEO TO LEAVE THEIR 
STUDIES IN ORDER TO TAKE THE PLACE OF BREADWINNERS IN 
THEIR FAMILIES WHO HAVE BEEN THROWN OUT OF WORKe 


ALONG WITH THIS GREATER DEMAND FOR SERVICE, 
HOWEVER, THERE 1S NO CORRESPONDING INCREASE IN MEMBERSHIP 
FEES, OR IN SUBSCRIPTIONS. MANY HOMES HAVE FOUND IT 
IMPOSSIBLE TO MEET EVEN THE SMALLEST MEMBERSHIP FEE FOR 
THEIR BOYSe YOUNG MEN IN RESIDENCE IN THE "Y" HAVE 
TEMPORARILY LOST THEIR JOBS ANO WHILE FINDING ANOTHER 
POSITION, HAVE HAD DIFFICULTY IN PAYING THEIR ROOM RENTS. 
STUDENTS IN THE EVENING COLLEGE HAVE FOUND IT HARD TO 
MEET THEIR PAYMENTS FOR TUITION FEES ON ACCOUNT OF RE- 
DUCED EARNINGS. THESE GENERAL CONDITIONS, COMBINEO WITH 
THE FACT THAT THE ASSOCIATION REMODELLED THE CENTRAL 
BUILDING AND COMPLETED THE CONSTRUCTION OF THE LARGEST 
OF ITS CONTEMPLATED THREE NEW BUILDINGS, HAVE MADE THE 
YEAR A RATHER TRYING ONE. UNUSUALLY HEAVY DEMANDS HAVE 
BEEN MADE UPON THE PATIENCE, TACT AND COURAGE OF ‘LAYMEN 
AND STAFF, BUT THROUGH THEIR EFFORTS THE YeMeCeAs WITH 
ITS MANY*SIDED WORK, HAS HAD A GOOD YEAR AND HAS PROVID- 
ED A STEADYING INFLUENCE AMONG OUR YOUNG PEOPLE WHICH 
HAS BEEN OF GREAT SIGNIFICANCE IN MAINTAINING THE MORALE 
OF THE COMMUNITY. 


FOREIGN SERVICE: 


ONLY IN TWO PREVIOUS YEARS HAS A LARGER AMOUNT 
OF MONEY BEEN SUBSCRIBED IN MONTREAL TOWARD THE MAINT= 
ENANCE OF CANADIAN SECRETARIES IN THE FOREIGN FIELD. 
THE AMOUNT RAISED BY US LAST YEAR WAS $21,720.11, A 
DECREASE OF $5,508.76 OVER THE PREVIOUS YEAR.

THE PREVAILING ECONOMIC DEPRESSION THROUGHOUT 

THE WORLD HAS ADVERSELY AFFECTED THE FINANCIAL SUPPORT 
OF THE FOREIGN SERVICE OF THE ASSOCIATION WITH THE RE=- 
SULT THAT THE BOOKS WERE CLOSED ON DECEMBER 30TH WITH A 
DEFICIT OF APPROXIMATELY $250,000.00. EVERY EFFORT IS 
BEING MADE TO SECURE THE NECESSARY FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO 
MAINTAIN THE ASSOCHATION'S INFLUENCE §N THE THIRTY@ONE 

_ COUNTRIES OF THE WORLD WHERE {T 13 OPERATING, AND AT THE 
SAME TIME EFFECT EVERY POSSIBLE ECONOMY IN ADMINISTRA~ 
ThONe

(ATLON WERE GIVEN BY MRe, FRANC/S HARMON, PRESIDENT OF THE

WeWe FRY, CHAIRMAN OF THE INTERNATIONAL FOREIGN SERVICE

MRe TeBe MACAULAY; BY MR. Acle MILLER, LAHORE; BY URe

INGS WERE HELD IN HONOR OF OUR PRESIDENT, MRe GERALD

WE ARE HAPPY TO REPORT THAT MRe Ge ERNEST TRUEMAN, 
a CANADIAN WHO HAS BEEN ONE OF THE LEADING SECRETARIES OF 
THE ASSOCIATION IN JAPAN FOR OVER TWENTY YEARS, HAS ACCEPT= 
£0 THE INVITATION OF OUR BOARD OR DIRECTORS TO BECOME ASSs- 
oClATE GENERAL SECRETARY, THIS APPOINTMENT TO TAKE EFFECT 
jn THE EARLY AUTUMN. 


IT 1S WORTHY OF NOTE THAT DRe SHERWOOD EDDY, UPON 
REACHING THE AGE OF RETIREMENT FROM ACTIVE SERVICE IN THE 
ASSOCIATION SECRETARYSHIP, TENDEREO HIS RESIGNATION AFTER 
THE SINGULARLY ABLE AND USEFUL DEDICATION OF THIRTY=FOUR® 
YEARS OF DISTINGUISHED SERVICE IN THE FOREIGN WORK OF THE 
ASSOCIATION ENTIRELY AT HIS OWN CHARGES. 


AS THIS REPORT IS BEING WRITTEN, WORD HAS COME 

FROM INDIA OF THE DEATH OF MR. KeTe PAUL, WHO FROM 1914 
UNTIL 1930 WAS NATIONAL SECRETARY OF THE ASSOCIATION. MRe 
PAUL WAS SELECTEO BY THE VICEROY TO BECOME A MEMBER OF 
“THE INDIAN ROUND TABLE CONFERENCE, WHICH ADJOURNED RECENT- 
LY IN LONOON, WHERE HE MADE A VALUABLE CONTRIBUTION TO 

THE DELIBERATIONS OF THAT BODY. BY HIS DEATH THE YeMoC.Ae 
IN INO!IA HAS LOST A TRUSTED LEADER AND THE INTERNATIONAL 
“MISSIONARY MOVEMENT ONE WHOSE COUNSEL WAS HIGHLY VALUED. 
HIS DEATH HAS OCCURRED AT A TIME WHEN HE HAD ENTERED UPON 

WHAT PROMISED TO BE A NEW PUBLIC CAREER OF GREAT USEFULNESS 
TO THE NATIONAL LIFE OF INDIA. 


PROGRESS OF NEW BUILDINGS: 


TWO MONTHS AFTER THE NEW SOUTHWESTERN BRANCH 
BUILDING WAS OPENED, THE CONTRACT WAS SIGNED FOR THE CON} 
. STRUCTION OF THE TWELVE STOREY EVENING COLLEGE ANO RESID- 
ENCE BUILDING ON STANLEY STREET AND THE REMODELLING OF 
THE EXISTING BUILDING ON DRUMMOND STREET WHICH WAS OPENED 
in 1912. THE PROJECT WAS AN UNUSUALLY DIFFICULT ONE FROM 
AN ENGINEERING AND ARCHITECTURAL POINT OF VIEW. DUE TO 
THE FACT THAT THE PRESENT BUILDING WAS ON PILES, ANXIETY 
was FELT AS TO THEIR CONDITION WHEN THEY WERE EXPOSED IN 
ORDER TO EFFECT THE NECESSARY HOOK-UP WITH THE NEW BUILDING. 


- FROM AN ADMINISTRATIVE POINT OF VIEW, TO CONTIN- 
UE THE OPERATION OF THE CENTRAL BRANCH, WITH SOME 3,000 
MEMBERS AND THE HOST OF TRANSIENTS WHO STREAMED INTO OUR 
BUILDING DAILY, WHILE THE RE=PIPING OF THE ENTIRE BUILO- 
ING, THE RE*ARRANGING OF ROOMS, PLASTERING, PAINTING AND 
PLUMBING WORK WAS BEING CARRIED OUT, WAS A TASK OF GREAT 
MAGNITUDE. 


IT REQUIRED A GOOD DEAL OF COURAGE FOR THE BOARD 
OF DIRECTORS, IN THE FACE OF ECONOMIC CONOITLONS WHICH 
WERE DELAYING PAYMENTS ON ACCOUNT OF BUILDING FUND PLEDGES, 
TO FACE SO HEAVY AN OBLIGATION AS THE EXPENDITURE OF 
NEARLY $1,000,000.00 WHICH THIS PROJECT INVOLVED. 


IT WAS, HOWEVER, A MATTER OF GREAT URGENCY THAT 
THE OLD BOILER ROOM EQUIPMENT BE REPLACED AND THE HOT 


BATER PEPCS IAROVGHOUT THE SUILOING BE RENEWEO; ALSO, 
THAT THE NEW LABORATORIES AND SOME OF THE NEW CLASS- 
ROOMS SHOULD BE COMPLETED BY OCTOBER IST IN ORDER THAT 
STUDENTS WHO WERE TAKING THE FULL HIGH SCHOOL COURSE 

IN THE COLLEGE SHOULD NOT HAVE THEIR EVENING STUDIES 
INTERRUPTED. _THAT THE COLLEGE WAS ABLE TO OPEN AT THE 
BEGINNING OF THE FALL TERM WITH AN EVEN GREATER ENROL~ 
MENT THAN LAST YEAR REFLECTS GREAT CREDIT UPON ALL CON- 
CERNED. AS A MATTER OF FACT, THE TRANSFORMATION WROUGHT 
IN THE OLD BUILDING DURING THE SUMMER MONTHS, ESPECIAL- 
LY ON THE THIRD FLOOR, WAS AN AMAZING ONE AND MADE THE 
COLLEGE ONE OF THE FINEST EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS IN 
QUR CITY. ' 


SOME THREE MONTHS LATER THE REMODELLING OF THE 
CENTRAL BRANCH WAS COMPLETED AND MADE A NOTABLE IMPROVE- 
MENT IN ITS FACILITIES. IMPORTANT CHANGES IN THE MAIN 
ENTRANCE WAS A MUCH MORE ATTRACTIVE AND USEFUL SOCIAL 
LOBBY AND MEMBERS’ SOCIAL ROOM. OTHER IMPROVEMENTS IN- 
CLUDED THE BETTER ARRANGEMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE OFFICES; 
NEW CHECKING ROOM FACILITIES; REMODELLING OF THE AUDITOR- 
1UM WITH A NEW FOYER AT THE ENTRANCE; NEW ORESSING ROOMS 
BEHIND THE AUDITORIUM STAGE; NEW LOCKER ROOMS AND SHOW- 
ER BATHS FOR BOYS, MEN, AND THE BUSINESS AND PROFESSION= 
AL MEN'S CLUB; TWO HANDICRAFT ROOMS FOR BOYS; THREE NEW 
HANOBALL COURTS; NEW CHESS AND CHECKER TASLES IN THE 
BILLIARD ROOM; MODERN SODA FOUNTAIN AND LUNCHEONETTE; 
AND COMPLETE EQUIPMENT FOR A NEW INDIVIDUAL HEALTH SERV= 
(CE ROOM WITH TWO ULTRA VIOLET LAMPS, AN INFRA RED LAMP, 
AN ELECTRIC BATH CABINET, AND A MASSAGE TASLE ALL IN 
CHARGE OF A SWEDISH MASSEUR. 


ON MARCH 31ST, THE CONTRACT WAS COMPLETED AND 
THE BUILDING READY FOR THE NUMEROUS PROGRAM EVENTS WHICH 
CULMINATED IN THE FORMAL OPENING ON SUNDAY,APRIL 26THe 


THE COMPLETION OF THE BUILDING MARKED AN INTER 

ESTING AND UNIQUE MILESTONE IN THE ASSOCIATION'S HISTORY. 

IT 1S UNTERESTING IN THAT THE BUILDING 1S LOCATED IN 
THE LARGEST CITY IN CANADA AND 1S THE LARGEST ASSOCIA= 
TION BUILDING IN THE DOMINION. IT IS UNIQUE, BECAUSE 
OF THE INTIMATE RELATION WHICH THE RESIDENCE ROOMS AND 
COLLEGE HAVE TO OUR EIGHT BRANCHES, IT BEING THE POLICY 
OF THEASSOCIATION TO CENTRALIZE ITS RESIDENCE ROOMS AND 
FORMAL EDUCATIONAL WORKe 


,WE DESIRE TO RECORD THAT THE METROPOLITAN BUILO= 
ING COMMITTEE, WHO WERE RESPONSIBLE FOR THIS PROJECT, 
AS WELL AS THE OTHER BUILDINGS, HAVE ALREADY HELD SEV- 
ENTY FORMAL MEETINGS AND A MUCH LARGER NUMBER OF {NFORM=- 
AL MEETINGS. 


AS WAS THE CASE IN THE SOUTHWESTERN BRANCH, THE 
NEW BUILDING WAS COMBINED ART AND COLOR WITH UTILITY IN 
A MASTERFUL WAY. IN THE ASSOCIATION BUILDINGS OF TO-DAY 
AN EARNEST ATTEMPT 1S BEING MADE TO SECURE AN ARTISTIC 
AND HOMELIKE ATMOSPHERE WITH THE RESULT THAT A REF INE@ 
MENT 1S TAKtNG PLACE IN BOTH ASSOCIATION EQUIPMENT AND ; 
PROGRAM, WHICH, UNDOUBTEDLY, WILL BE REFLECTED {IN THE 
CHARACTER OF OUR CONSTITUENTS. 


THE BUILDING 1S MECHANICALLY EFFICIENT IN ITS 
HEATING, LIGHTING ANO VENTILATION EQUIPMENT, THE HEATING 
PLANT BEING A GIFT OF ONE OF THE LARGER CORPORATIONS ANDO 
REPRESENTING AN IMPORTANT FINANCIAL SAVING TO THE Assoce 


1ATIONe 


THE SKY*LINES “OF THE CITY IN RECENT YEARS HAVE 
BEEN MARKEO BY CATHEDRALS OF COMMERCE AND FINANCE, AND 
iT 1S FITTING THAT THE YOUNG MEN'S CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATION 
SHOULO MAKE ITS CONTRIBUTION TO THE ARCHITECTURE OF THE 
DAY BY ERECTING CATHEDRALS OF YOUTH. 


RESIDENCE BUILDING: 


DURING THE YEAR THAT HAS ELAPSED, OVER 3,200 
DIFFERENT MEN OCCUPIED OUR RESIDENCE ROOMS IN THE DRUMM- 
OND STREET, WESTMOUNT AND NORTH BRANCH BUILDINGS, THERE 
BEING AN AVERAGE OF 215 MEN EACH NIGHT. ON THE 26TH OF 
FEBRUARY, FORTY*FOUR ROOMS WERE ADDED TO THE ACCOMMODA- 
TION, MAKING THE FIRST ADDITION TO OUR RESIDENCE ACCOMM- 
ODATION SINCE 1912, 


THE ASSOCIATION NOW HAS A TOTAL OF 624 ROOMS AS

IT SHOULD BE RECALLED THAT 80 PER CENT OF THE 
MEN LIVING IN THE "Y" ARE BETWEEN THE AGES OF EIGHTEEN 
ANO TWENTY-FIVE YEARS OF AGE, THE AVERAGE BEING 22. 
THIS RESIDENCE ROOMS SERVICE 1S OF INEST IMABLE VALUE 
TO THE COMMUNITYe. THOUGHTFUL PEOPLE RECOGNIZE AT ONCE 
THAT THE PROBLEM OF LONELINESS IN A GREAT CITY IS A 
MOST SERIOUS ONE FOR YOUNG MEN. FROM THEPOINT OF VIEW 
OF THE CONSERVATION OF CHARACTER, IT 9S OF THE GREATEST 
IMPORTANCE FOR A CITY TO MAKE PROVISION FOR A FRIENDLY 
PLACE OF RESIDENCE FOR YOUNG MEN TO MEET OTHERS ON A 
HIGH PLANE OF LIFE. 


FINANCE AND PROPERTY: 


DURING OUR FISCAL YEAR THE BALANCE OF THE FUNDS 
REQUIRED TO ENABLE US TO REACH OUR BUILDING FUND GOAL 


OF ONE ANO ONE©HALF MILLION DOLLARS, AND THUS SECURE THE 
$80,000.00 CONDITIONAL GIFTS PROMISED BY THREE FRIENDS , 
oF THE ASSOCIATION, WERE SUBSCRIBED OR UNDERWRITTEN. THE . 
SECURING OF THESE PLEDGES DOES NOT SOLVE THE ASSOCIATION'S 
FINANCIAL PROBLEMS IN CONNECTION WITH OUR NEW BUILDINGS 

AS WE MUST INCREASE OUR MORTGAGE LOAN FROM THE $240,000.00 
CONTEMPLATED IN 1928 TO $400,000.00, AS WELL AS MAKE COLL- 
ECTION OF THE $267,000.00 OUTSTANDING IN ORDER TO ERECT 

THE NOTRE DAME DE GRACE BUILDING AND THUS COMPLETE OUR 
BUILDING PROGRAM. 


OUR MORTGAGE LOAN HAS BEEN ARRANGED AT A FAVORABLE 
INTEREST RATE, ANDO CARRIES THE PRIVILEGE OF REDUCTION IN 
ANY YEAR UP TO $50,000.00 IN THE EVENT OF OUR FORTUNATELY 
BEING IN RECEIPT OF FUNDS FROM LEGACIES OR ANY OTHER " 
SOURCES. THE INCREASE IN OUR LOAN IS DUE TO THE DECISION . 
OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS TO PLACE TWO ADDITIONAL FLOORS 
OF DORMITORIES ON THE STANLEY STREET BUILDING, AT A COST 
OF $75,000-¢00, AND AN INCREASE IN THE COST OF REMODELLING 
THE DRUMMOND STREET BUILDING. 


YouR FINANCE COMMITTEE HAS BEEN SUCCESSFUL IN NEG@- 
OTIATING LOCALLY A NEW AND FAVORABLE FIRE INSURANCE RATE 
ON THE CENTRAL ANDO SOUTHWESTERN BRANCH BUILDINGS. 


DURING THE YEAR THE PROPERTY OWNED BY THE ASSOC~ 
1ATION ON WELLINGTON STREET, POINT STe CHARLES, WAS SOLO, 
AS THE PURPOSES FOR WHICH THE LOTS HAD BEEN BOUGHT DID NOT 
NOW EXIST. 


Two LEGACIES HAVE BEEN RECEIVED SINCE OUR LAST 
ANNUAL MEETING, ONE OF 30 POUND FROM THE LATE JOSEPH ALLAN 
OF HADDINGTON, AND ONE FROM THE LATE MR. AsAe AYER OF 
$500.00. 


WE ARE PLEASED TO REPORT THAT LAST MAY THE 
FEDERAL GOVERNMENT BROUGHT DOWN LEGISLATION INCLUDING THE 
YeMeCoAe AMONG THE OBJECTS. TO. WHICH. GIFTS ARE DEOUCTIBLE 
FROM INCOME TAX RETURNS 


ONE OF THE OUTSTANDING. ACHIEVEMENTS OF THE TWELVE 
MONTHS' PERIOD WAS THE RE*ESTABLISHMENT OF OUR ANNUAL 
FINANCIAL SUPPORT, THE LAST MAINTENANCE FUND CAMPAIGN 
HAVING BEEN HELO IN: 19276 


THE REQUIREMENTS FOR THE YEAR 1928 AND 1929 WERE 
INCLUDED IN THE BUILDING FUND OBJECTIVE>

ORGANIZATION OF 350 WORKERS UNDER THE LEADERSHIP OF

SUBSCRIBERSe

MEMBERSHIP: 


THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE ASSOCIATION ON MARCH 31ST 
was 6,479 AS COMPARED WITH 7,088, BEING A DECREASE OF 
610 MEMBERS OR 8 PER CENT. IT WAS FREELY. PREDICTED 
THAT IT WAS NOT PRACTICABLE TO OPERATE THE CENTRAL 
BRANCH DURING THE REMODELLING PERIOD. THE FACT, HOWEVER, 

THAT THE CENTRAL BRANCH LOST ONLY 282 MEMBERS DURING 
THE YEAR 1S A TRIBUTE TO THE LOYALTY OF ITS CONSTITUENCY. 
THE MEMBERSHIP, DECREASE IN THE OTHER BRANCHES REFLECTED 
THE CHANGING ECONOMIC CONDITIONS IN THEIR RESPECTIVE 
COMMUNITBESe

THESE FIGURES, OF COURSE, DO NOT INCLUDE THE HUNOD- 
REOS OF YOUNG MEN AND BOYS WHO JOIN THE ASSOCIATION ONLY 
FOR THE SUMMER MONTHS OR TO TAKE ADVANTAGE OF OUR -SHORT 
TERM MEMBERSHIP, NOR DO THEY INCLUDE THE THOUSANDS OF YOUNG 
PEOPLE WHO PARTICIPATED IN OUR COMMUNITY PROGRAMS WHICH ARE 
NOT RESTRICTED TO MEMBERSHIP IN THE "Y", NOR DO THEY HAVE 
ANY REFERENCE TO THE LARGE NUMBER OF PERSONS, ESPECIALLY 
IN VERDUN, WHO USE THE ASSOCIATION AS A COMMUNITY CENTRE, 
NOR THE CONSTANT STREAM OF NEWCOMERS TO OUR CITY WHO ARE 
RENDERED AN IMPORTANT SERVICE OF A MISCELLANEOUS CHARACT- 
ER WITHOUT THEIR SEING REQUIRED TO BECOME MEMBERS OF THE 
ASSOCIATION. 


IN VIEW OF THE LARGE ADDITION TO THE ASSOCIATION'S 
EQUIPMENT IN THE STANLEY STREET BUILOING, WE MUST FACE 
THE NEW YEAR WITH THE HIGH RESOLVE TO NOT ONLY WIN BACK 
THE MEMBERS LOST IN THE PERIOD OF BUILDING CONSTRUCTION 
BUT TO SECURE THE NUMBER REQUIRED TO FULLY OCCUPY OUR NEW 
FACILITIES. SHOULD THE BOARD DECIDE THAT IN VIEW OF ALL 
THE CIRCUMSTANCES WE SHOULO HAVE A CITY-WIDE MEMBERSHIP 
CAMPAIGN IN THE FALL, WITH A UNIFORM SCALE OF MEMBERSHIP 
FEES, GIVING THE RIGHT TO MEMBERS OF A GIVEN 8RANCH TO 
USE THE FACILITIES OF ANY OR ALL OF THE BRANCHES, AS HAS 
BEEN DONE IN OTHER METROPOLITAN CITIES, -IT -!S HOPED THAT 
THERE WILL BE THE USUAL LOYAL RESPONSE ON THE PART OF 
OUR WORKERS. 


THE ROCHESTER ASSOCIATION HAVE FOUND, THROUGH A 
SCIENTIFIC STUDY, THAT MEMBERS JOINING THE ASSOCIATION 
OURING CAMPAIGNS CONTINUE IN THE MEMBERSHIP, ON AN AVER- 
AGE, AS LONG AS THOSE WHO JOIN IN THE DAILY COURSE oF 
THE ASSOCIATION'S LIFE. 


STAFF _TRAINING: 


ONE OF THE VITAL TASKS CONFRONTING THE MODERN 
YOUNG MEN'S CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATION tS THE TRAINING OF ITS 
SECRETARIATe THE WORK WHICH HAS BEEN DONE IN THIS FIELD 
IN PAST YEARS HAS BEEN MARKED BY A CREATIVE SPIRIT, FLEX- 
IBILITY OF METHOD, AND A DEVOTION WHICH MIGHT ALMOST BE 
CHARACTERIZED AS A CRUSADE. IT HAS BEEN A LONG AND 
DIFFICULT TASK TO RECRUIT AND TRAIN SUFFICIENT MEN OF THE 
RIGHT SPIRIT TO GIVE LEADERSHIP TO ALL ITS DEPARTMENTS. 


DURING THE PAST YEAR WE HAVE HAD PRECISELY THE 
SAME NUMBER OF SECRETARIES ON OUR REGULAR STAFF AS 
DURING THE YEAR PREVIOUS -- 33. SEVEN SECRETARIES ATT~ 
ENDEO THE TRIENNIAL CONFERENCE OF THE NORTH AMERICAN 
EMPLOYED OFFICERS OF THE ASSOCIATION HELO IN DETROIT IN 
MAY, TWO ATTENOEO THE SUMMER TRAINING SCHOOL AT LAKE 
COUCHICHING IN AUGUST; AND ONE ATTENDED THE SUMMER SCHOOL 
AT COLUMBIA UNIVERSITYe IN ADDITION, THREE SECRETARIES 
ATTENDEO THE ANNUAL MEETING OF THE NATIONAL COUNCIL AT 
NIAGARA FALLS; ONE ATTENDEO THE BOYS* WORK SECRETARIES* 
ASSOCIATION AT HAMILTON; ONE TOOK PART IN THE ORIENTATION 
WEEK AT THE SPRINGFIELD YeMeCeAe COLLEGE, AND TWO 
ATTENDED THE MEETINGS OF THE NATIONAL COUNCIL OF EDUC- 
ATION HELD IN DETROITe YOUR GENERAL SECRETARY ALSO 
ATTENDED A MEETING OF THE METROPOLITAN SECRETARIES' 
ASSOCIATION AT. NIAGARA FALLS. IN ADDITION TO THE ABOVE, 
A STAFF TRAINING INSTITUTE WAS HELD WEEKLY FOR THREE 
MONTHS UNDER THE LEADERSHIP OF DR. EoMe BEST, DR WeTeBe 
MITCHELL, ANO OTHERSe

KAMP_KANAWANA: 
THE SEASON OF 1930 WAS KNOWN IN OUR BoYS't CAMP 
AS "COMING OF AGE" YEAR. THE CAMP HAS BEEN IN OPERATION 
FOR TWENTY@ONE YEARS IN ITS PRESENT LOCATION ALTHOUGH, 
IN 1898, OR FORTY YEARS AGO, THE FIRST BOYS CAMP OF 
THE ASSOCIATION WAS OPENED AT LAC ST. JOSEPH. THE CAMP 
BIRTHDAY WAS FITTINGLY OBSERVED EARLY IN JULY, WHEN MR, 
WeJe HOLLIDAY, THE FIRST CAMP DIRECTOR, DELIVERED AN 
INSPIRING ADDRESS, AND MR. GNAEDINGER, THE FORMER 
PRESIDENT OF THE COMMITTEE, GAVE A TALK REMINISCENT OF 
THE DAYS WHEN A CAMP OF THIRTY=FIVE BOYS WAS CONSIDERED 
LARGE. THE SEASON JUST CLOSED ESTABLISHED A NEW HIGH 
MARK IN POINT OF ATTENDANCE, THERE BEING [512 BOY WEEKS, 
AN INCREASE OF 432 OVER LAST YEAR; AND 447 BOYS, COMPAR- 
ED WITH 347. THE BOYS CAME FROM ALL PARTS OF MONTREAL 
AND SUBURBS, ORMSTOWN, OTTAWA, STRATFORD, NAPANEE, NEW 
YORK, STe LOUIS, WASHINGTON, DeCo, NEW HAVEN AND TEXAS. 
THE USUAL ACTIVE AND HELPFUL PROGRAM CHARACTERIZED THE 
WORK OF THE YEAR.

TOTALLED 159 WHICH WAS A DECREASE OF 46 OVER THE PREV=- 
1QUS YEAR. THE PROGRAM FOR THE YEAR WAS CARRIED 
THROUGH ALONG LINES WHICH HAVE BEEN FOLLOWED DURING

THE YEAR JUST ENDED SAW A REPITITION OF THE USUAL 
FINE INTER=BRANCH CO-OPERATION AND COMPETITION, ANO A DEF- 
INITE GROWTH IN ESPRIT DE CORPS. 


EARLY. IN THE FALL, REPRESENTATIVES OF THE CABINETS 
OF EACH BRANCH MET IN CONFERENCE AT THE SOUTHWESTERN BRANCH, 
UNDER THE LEADERSHIP OF MR. WeRe COOK, NATIONAL BOYS’ WORK 
SECRETARY. THE RESULT WAS TO GIVE A MORE DEFINITE CITY- 
WIDE CONSCIOUSNESS TO OUR WHOLE WORK, AND PUT A GREATER 
SHARE OF RESPONSIBILITY ON THE BOYS THEMSELVES. 


FATHER AND SON BANQUETS WERE HELD SIMULTANEOUSLY 
AT WESTMOUNT, NORTH, MOUNT ROYAL AVENUE BRANCH, AND CENTRAL 
BRANCH. SPEAKERS WERE REV. JeW. CLARKE, DR. EeMeBEST, MRe 
ReHe DEAN, AND OR. E, LESLIE PIDGEON. THE TOTAL ATTENDANCE 
WAS ALMOST ONE THOUSAND FATHERS AND SONS~ 


INTER“BRANCH COMPETITION WAS EXEMPLIFIEO IN THE 
PING-PONG CHAMPIONSHIPS, WHEN THE WINNERS FROM EACH BRANCH 
WERE PITTED AGAINST THE OTHER WINNERS OF THEIR OWN AGEe 
CHAMPIONSHIPS WENT TO SOUTHWESTERN (TWO), CENTRAL AND 
NOTRE DAME DE GRACE. THE ANNUAL CITY*WI0E SWIMMING MEET 
WAS WON BY WESTMOUNT. A SEVEN@TEAM BASKETBALL LEAGUE, 

FOR BOYS UNDER WIGHTEEN YEARS OF AGE, WAS PARTICIPATED IN 

BY RAILROAD, NORTH, CENTRAL, MOUNT ROYAL, NOTRE DAME DE

VERY WORTHWHILE ACTIVITY. ; gh 


UNDOUBTEDLY THE EVENT WITH THE FINEST EDUCATIONAL 
VALUE 1S THE MONTREAL BoYS' HOBBY SHOW, WHICH WE HAVE 
SPONSORED SINCE PNEEPTION, THIS YEAR IT INCLUDED NOT 
ONLY THE BRANCHES OF THE YeMeCeAe BUT ALSO HAD THE OFFIC~ 
[AL ENOORSATION OF AND REPRESENTATION FROM THE BOY SCOUTS’ 
ASSOCIATION, THE YeMeHeAe, THE SALVATION ARMY LIFE SAV- 
in@ SCOUTS, THE WEREDALE Boys! HOME, AND THE KNIGHTS OF 
HONOUR OF STe JAMES UNITED CHURCHe THE OFFICIAL REPRE~ 
SENTATIVES OF BRANCHES AND CO-OPERATING ORGANIZATIONS 
COMPOSED THE HOBBY SHOW BOARD, AND WORKED DILIGENTLY AND 
EFFECTIVELY FROM EARLY IN DECEMBER TILL THE SHOW WAS 
ACTUALLY COMPLETED. THEY PLANNED THE BOOKLET,SECURED ' 
THE ADVERTISEMENTS, GOT COMPETITIVE PRICES ON PRINTING, 
LET THEIR CONTRACT, FOLLOWED THE BOOK THROUGH THE PRESS, 
ANO THEN DISTRIBUTED THE COPIES. THEY SECURED JUDGES 
ANO SPECIAL PRIZES FOR THEIR DEPARTMENTS. THE PRESIDENT 
ARRANGED FOR ONE OF HIS BOARD TO SPEAK BEFORE EACH OF 
THE SERVICE CLUBS, AND OBTAINED THE GRAND CHAMPIONSHIP 
Cups AND MEDALS FROM THE LIONS, THE GYRO, ANO KIWANIS 
CLUBS. THROUGH THE COURTESY OF THE PURPLE CIRCLE, THEY 
WERE ABLE TO BROADCAST SEVERAL ANNOUNCEMENTSOOF *THE 
EXHIBITION. FINALLY, THEY RECEIVED THE ENTRIES, SAW 
THEM JUDGED, POLICED THE SHOW WHILE IT WAS ON, AND 
SUPERVISED THE RETURN OF THE EXHIBITS TO THE EXHIBITORS. 
AN INNOVATION THIS YEAR WAS THE ADMISSION OF GIRLS TO 
ELIGIBILITY AS EXHIBITORS. THE RESULTS WOULD JUSTIFY 
EXPANSION IN THIS DIRECTION, IN ALL, THERE WERE ABOUT 
FOUR HUNDRED EXHIBITORS, WITH OVER ONE THOUSAND EXHIBITS. 


THROUGHOUT OUR CITY WORK WE FIND BOYS ASSUMING 
REAL RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE PROGRAM OF THEIR BRANCHES, 
AND WE BELIEVE THEY ARE TRAINING THEMSELVES FOR POSI- 
TIONS OF LEADERSHIP IN THE DAYS AHEAD.

THE MANNER OF CONDUCTION ALL THE FEATURES OF THE MANY 
SIDED PROGRAM OF CHARACTER DEVELOPMENT.

CITY-WIDE RELATIONSHIPS: 


THE LEADERS OF THE ASSOCIATION HAVE REALIZED 

FOR MANY YEARS THAT THE YeMeCeAe IS ONE OF THE MANY 

» AGENCIES AT WORK IN THE WORLD WITH THE IDEA OF ESTAB- 
LISHING A REIGN OF RIGHTEOUSNESS, AND TO THIS END HAS 
SOUGHT TO ALLY ITSELF TO MANY ORGANIZATIONS WORKING 
FOR BETTER SOCIAL, EDUCATIONAL AND RELIGIOUS CONDITIONS 
IN OUR CITYe AS A RESULT, MUCH HAS BEEN ACCOMPLISHED IN 
COOPERATION WHICH WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE BEEN IMPOSSIBLE, 
IN SOME CASES THE PART THE YeMeCeAe HAS PLAYED HAS BEEN 
A RELATIVELY SMALL ONE; AT OTHER TIMES IT HAS MADE A 
CONTRIBUTION OF FIRST IMPORTANCE.

METROPOLITAN PHYSICAL EDUCATION: 

THE ASSOCIATION HAS ALWAYS RECOGNIZED THE CLOSE 
AFFINITY BETWEEN A HEALTHY BODY ANO A CLEAN CHARACTER, 
AND HAS ENDEAVORED TO PROVIDE WHOLESOME PHYSICAL ACTIVI- 
TIES AND ATHLETIC RECREATION FACILITIES FOR BOYS AND MEN 
OF ALL AGES. 


THE GYMNASIUM CLASSES HAVE CONTINUED TO BE THE 
BACKBONE OF GUR PROGRAM, ORGANIZED AND INSTRUCTED GROUPS 
RECEIVING CAREFULLY PLANNED AND PROGRESSIVE TRAINING IN 
BODY=BUILDING, HEALTH PRODUCING AND MUSCULAR EFFICIENCY 
EXERCISES. THESE CLASSES, WHILE SERVING THE NEEDS OF THE 
MEMBERS WHO DO NOT WISH ANY OTHER FORM OF PHYSICAL EXER@= 
CISE, ALSO SERVE TO INTRODUCE OTHERS TO THE INDIVIDUAL 
AND TEAM RECREATIONAL FACILITIES PROVIDEDe THE SPORTS 
ANO GAMES PROGRAMME OF THE ASSOCIATION IS BECOMING INC 
REASINGLY POPULAR.

SOUTHWESTERN: 


THE OUTSTANDING ADVANCE IN THE ASSOCIATION'S SERV- 
{CE DURING THE YEAR WHICH HAS JUST CLOSED WAS THE COMPLETE 
OPERATION FOR TWELVE MONTHS OF THE NEW SOUTHWESTERN BRANCH 
BUILDING LOCATED IN VERDUNe THE CONTRIBUTION MADE TO THE 
LIFE OF THE COMMUNITY HAS JUSTIFIED IN FULL MEASURE THE 
INVESTMENT OF TIME AND MONEY WHICH WAS MADE IN THIS BUILDING. 


IN ADDITION TO THE INTENSIVE PROGRAM CARRIED ON 
THROUGHOUT THE YEAR FOR YOUNG WOMEN AND GIRLS AND YOUNG MEN 
AND BOYS, THE BUILDING HAS BEEN, IN AN UNUSUAL SENSE, A 
COMMUNITY CENTRE. THE AUDITORIUM HAS BEEN USED BY TWENTY= 
TWO DIFFERENT ORGANIZATIONS; WHILE OTHER ROOMS IN THE BUILD=- 
ING HAVE BEEN USEO BY AS MANY MORE. THE WORK HAS HAD THE 
ACTIVE CO-OPERATION AND SUPPORT OF THE CITY COUNCIL AND CITY 
OFFICIALS OF VERDUN, THE SCHOOL TRUSTEES, PRINCIPALS AND 
TEACHERS OF THE PROTESTANT SCHOOLS, THE MINISTERS, THE 
PRESS, MERCHANTS, INDUSTRIES AND CITIZENS OF THE COMMUN@ 
ITYe 


THE MAIN ADDITIONS TO THE EQUIPMENT WERE THE CON]- 
STRUCTION OF SIX TENNIS COURTS, THE LEVELLING FOR THE PLAY- 
ING FIELD WHICH ADJOINS THE BUILDING, AND THE OPENING OF 
THE Cole WILLIAMS MEMORIAL LIBRARY, THE LATTER MADE POSSIBLE 
THROUGH THE GENEROUS GIFT OF THREE THOUSAND DOLLARS FROM 
MRSe CeTe WILLIAMS IN MEMORY OF HER HUSBAND, A FORMER PRES-= 
IDENT OF OUR ASSOCIATIONe LOCATED IN A COMMUNITY WHERE 
THERE 1S NO PUBLIC LIBRARY, OVER TWO THOUSAND VOLUMES HAVE 
BEEN PLACEO UPON THE BOOK=SHELVES, INCLUDING AN UNUSUALLY 
FINE SELECTION IN THE FIELOS OF ART, ECONOMICS, RELIGION, 
NATURE STUDY, POETRY, BIOGRAPHY, HISTORY AND FICTION, WITH 
A SPECIAL DEPARTMENT FOR CHILDRENe THIS LIBRARY HAS MADE 
A OISTINCT CONTRIBUTION TO THE EDUCATIONAL AND CULTURAL 
ASPECTS OF THE ASSOCIATION'S PROGRAM AND THE COMMUNITY 
AT LARGE. 
¢ AMONG THE OUTSTANDING PROGRAM EVENTS OF THE YEAR 
WERE THE NORTHERN ELECTRIC COMPANY EVENING WHEN NEARLY 
SIX HUNDRED EMPLOYEES SPENT AN ENJOYABLE EVENING USING 
THE GYMNASIUM, SWIMMING POOL, BILLIARD ROOM AND SOCIAL 
FACILITIES, CONCLUDING THE EVENING WITH A SOCIAL DANCE; 
THE SCHOOL TEACHERS TEA IN OCTOBER WHEN OVER ONE HUNDREO

IONAL CONFERENCE OF REPRESENTATIVES OF YeM.CeA'S FROM

INCLUDEO IN THE ABOVE NAMES IS THAT OF THE LATE 
MR. ABNER KINGMAN, PRESIDENT OF THE ASSOCIATION FROM 
1890 To 1892, WHO FOR FIFTY-FIVE YEARS WAS AN INTERESTED 
ANO HELPFUL MEMBER OF THE YoMeCeAe, SERVED ON ITS VARIOUS 
COMMITTEES, WAS LATER ELECTED TO THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS, 
AND SUBSEQUENTLY BECAME.A MEMBER OF THE INTERNATIONAL 
COMMITTEE. DURING THE WORLD WAR HE RENDERED AN OUTSTAND- 
ING SERVICE TO THE ASSOCIATION IN ITS SERVICE TO THE 
CANADIAN OVERSEAS FORCES, AND DURING THE YEARS 1915 To 
1918 ACTED AS CHAIRMAN OF THE OVERSEAS EXECUTIVE COMMI- 
TYEE OF THE YeMeCeoAs AN APPROPRIATE RESOLUTION OF 


APPRECIATION OF HIS LIFE AND SERVICE, AND SYMPATHY. WITH 
HIS FAMILY IN THEIR GREAT LOSS, HAS BEEN RECORDEO IN 
THE MINUTES OF THE METROPOLITAN BOARD. 


MRe KINGMAN*S NAME WILL BE PERPETUATED IN THE 
ASSOCIATION THROUGH THE ANNUAL AWARD OF FIVE SCHOLAR] 
SHIPS IN OUR SIR GEORGE WILLIAMS COLLEGE AND IN THE 
"ABNER KINGMAN" MEMORIAL LECTURE HALL ON THE SECOND FLOOR, 


APPRECIATION: 


THERE. ARE MANY FACTORS WHICH COMBINE TO MAKE 

POSSIBLE A SUCCESSFUL YEAR'S WORK IN THE YeleCeAe WE 
- ARE GRATEFUL TO THE MANY FRIENDS WHO HAVE CONTRIBUTED 
GENEROUSLY OF THEIR FINANCIAL RESOURCES; TO THE WORKERS 
IN THE MAINTENANCE AND OTHER CAMPAIGNS; TO MEMBERS OF 
BOARDS AND COMMITTEES FOR THEIR FREQUENT COUNSEL, GUID- 
ANCE AND SERVICE; TO THE MANY VOLUNTEERS WHO HAVE SERV=- 
ED AS FRIENDLY COUNSELLORS OF CLUBS; INTERVIEWERS; 
SPEAKERS; TEACHERS; INTERPRETERS; MINISTERS; TO THE PRESS; 
THE MEMBERS OF. THE LEADERS’ CORPS; THE STAFF; TO THE 
CHURCHES; THE WOMEN'S AUXILIARIES; THE PROTESTANT BOARD 
OF SCHOOL COMMISSIONERS; RAILROAD AND OTHER CORPORATIONS; 
PARKS AND PLAYGROUND ASSOCIATION; THE YOUNG WOMEN'S 
CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATION AND MANY OTHER CO*OPERATING AGENC= 
(ES, ABOVE ALL, WE ARE IN HUMILITY GRATEFUL To GoD FOR 
HIS BLESSING AND POWER. 


CONCLUS ION: 


THE EDITOR OF THE CALCUTTA "STATESMAN" SAID 
RECENTLY THAT "THE Y.M,CeAe 1S ONE OF THE GREAT FACTS 
UPON WHICH THE WORLD HAS MADE UP ITS MIND, PRONOUNCING 
IT TO BE A BENEFICENT INFLUENCE. WE ARE PROUD OF ITS 
RECORD, WE ARE PROUD OF THE WORK IT IS DOING NOT ONLY 
IN INOFA BUT. WHEREVER IT HAS BEEN ESTABLISHED. WE 
BELIEVE THAT IF THE. YeMeCeAe WERE DESTROYED TO-MORROW 
IT WOULD BE NECESSARY AGAIN TO INVENT IT, FOR. IT FILLS 
AN ESSENTIAL. PLACE IN SOCIAL AND RELIGIOUS ORGANIZATION», 


RESPECTFULLY SUBMITTED, 


JeW. BEATON
